solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Loaf a bit, dancing with a cat

indicators.note: dancing has the letters of the two short phrases skip about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone idles a little, doing a dance with the family cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaf' looks like a verb meaning idle, alongside 'a bit'; it is the noun, a kind of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciabatta is a flat Italian bread, a specific example of a loaf.

clue.text: Having rooms on the house torn away?

parts.note: rent is the past participle of rend, meaning ripped
free here means loose, escaped, got away

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a house whose rooms have been ripped off it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the house' is the idiom for at no charge, not a roof; 'torn away' read as two words gives the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Lodging without paying anything to a landlord is the sense; 'on the house' is the idiom for free of charge.

clue.text: Touch suspicious, not seeing any resistance to win, or nearly

indicators.note: not seeing any says every instance of the following letter is dropped from what comes before

parts.note: to touch is to reach, as in reaching the ceiling
suspicious means wary
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance; 'any' takes it from both words

explanation.surface: A gambler, slightly wary, wants a bet that pays out on a win or a near thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not seeing any resistance' drops the R from both REACH and WARY, leaving EACH and WAY.
explanation.definitionFit: An each-way bet in British horse racing pays if the horse wins or is placed, finishing just behind the winner.

clue.text: Republican nobody introduces lunchtime mischief in DC

indicators.note: introduces puts the word for nobody in front of the party letter

parts.note: nobody means no one

explanation.surface: A political scandal: an unnamed Republican sets up some midday misbehaviour in Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's order puts Republican first, but 'introduces' has nobody come before it.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for a sexual liaison squeezed into the midday break; DC points to US usage.

clue.text: Jellied preparations like shots

parts.note: like means as, in the sense of similarly to
shots are photographs, pics for short

explanation.surface: Jellies that look like photographs, or like shots of liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly in which meats or eggs are set, so the plural names jellied dishes.

clue.text: About time the best should stop efforts to see horny old beasts

indicators.note: should stop means these pieces plug the middle of the word for efforts

parts.note: efforts are attempts, tries
C is short for circa, Latin for about
an era is a period of time
the tops is slang for the very best

explanation.surface: Palaeontology: a period of time and the best digs halt efforts to find ancient horned creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: These were three-horned dinosaurs, so they are both literally horned and long extinct.

clue.text: What's moved passes time on clock, with First Lady keeping Mohammed's wife inside

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the time letter above the rest
inside puts the combined names into the word for clock

parts.note: to clock someone is slang for to hit them

indicators.note: keeping means the first lady holds the other wife within her

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis
Ayesha (Aisha) was a wife of the Prophet Mohammed

explanation.surface: A clock-themed riddle about an American First Lady harbouring the Prophet's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's moved' is a motion put to a vote; the Speaker's phrase announces that the vote in favour has carried it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the parliamentary formula declaring that a motion has been carried by the votes in favour.

clue.text: American force in tatters, so rope deployed

indicators.note: deployed means the letters are spread out and arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A US military force in rags, so rope is brought into service.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the highway patrol police of a US state, a law-enforcement force.

clue.text: Children's writer rebuffed the northern Norwegian one

indicators.note: rebuffed means pushed back, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: in northern English dialect 'the' is shortened to t'
Henrik Ibsen is the Norwegian writer, one like the children's author

explanation.surface: A children's author snubs a northern Norwegian.
explanation.walkthrough: Ibsen is the famous Norwegian playwright; 'one' points back to 'writer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Nesbit wrote The Railway Children and other classic stories for young readers.

clue.text: Impede recall of alkalinity measurement involving caustic soda ingredient

indicators.note: recall means calling back, so everything is read in reverse
involving means the measurement wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: pH measures acidity or alkalinity
an acid is caustic
Na is the chemical symbol for sodium, the soda in caustic soda

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: an alkalinity reading that involves an ingredient of caustic soda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caustic soda' looks like one substance, sodium hydroxide, but the two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: To handicap is to hamper or put at a disadvantage, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Hardly anyone said that's a relief

indicators.note: said means the interjection is spoken and heard as another word

parts.note: phew is the exclamation of relief

explanation.surface: Barely anybody remarked that they were relieved.
explanation.definitionFit: A small number, hardly any people at all, is the quantity sense.

clue.text: Storey remodelled by secretive person

indicators.note: remodelled suggests building work, here rearranging the letters of storey

explanation.surface: A secretive person has remodelled a floor of their house.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps their mouth shut, like a closed shellfish, is called this in British idiom.

clue.text: Copper part of turret's erratically rotating

indicators.note: rotating says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the letters lie inside the following words, across the end of one into the next

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A copper ornament forms part of a turret that turns erratically.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Copper part' as the definition, but 'part of' is the signal that the letters sit inside 'turret's erratically'; the definition is 'Copper' alone, a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A copper is British slang for a police officer, whose job includes making arrests.

clue.text: Female on farm following zigzag path?

definitions.meaning: a female sheep is a common farm animal
heading east, west, then east again, read as compass letters, is a zigzag route

explanation.surface: A female farm animal wanders along a zigzag track.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sheep is the farm animal; the second reading spells the compass points East, West, East.

clue.text: Recorded over silence with one bar level topping another

definitions.text: with one bar level topping another

indicators.note: over means the recording is made over, on top of and around, the silence

parts.note: recorded means taped
sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A recording made over silence features a musical bar topping another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests music after 'Recorded'; it is a straight crossbar on an upright, like the letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaped like the letter T: a horizontal crossbar resting on top of a vertical one.

clue.text: Letter from company offering connections to the north

indicators.note: to the north, in a down clue, means the letters run upwards

parts.note: an ISP is an internet service provider, a company that connects you

explanation.surface: A letter arrives from a firm offering links to the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Psi is the twenty-third letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Sister almost comprehending Spanish is a great musician

indicators.note: comprehending means taking in, enclosing the next piece
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a Sister is a senior nurse, a matron
ES is the abbreviation for Spanish (español)

explanation.surface: A nun nearly understands that Spanish is a great musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sister' reads as a sibling or nun; it is the hospital rank, a matron.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestro is the title given to a distinguished musician, especially a conductor.

clue.text: Buffoon in contact with six-footer having correspondence

parts.note: a buffoon is a fool, an ass
on means touching, in contact with
an ant is an insect with six legs

explanation.surface: A fool, in touch with a very tall person, carries on a correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person; it is an insect with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody it describes words whose vowel sounds correspond or rhyme partly.

clue.text: Sir, maths needs revising pronto

indicators.note: needs revising means the letters must be reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A pupil tells the teacher that maths revision is needed urgently.
explanation.definitionFit: Briskly or quite quickly in British informal usage, matching pronto as quickly.

clue.text: Old fool and minister climbing, not having the head for it?

definitions.text: not having the head for it?

indicators.note: climbing, in a down clue, means the letters read upwards

parts.note: git is British slang for a fool
Rev is short for reverend, a minister

explanation.surface: An old fool and a vicar go climbing, though one lacks the stomach for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'a head for heights': climbing is the activity in question.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the dizziness that strikes at heights, so a sufferer lacks a head for climbing.

clue.text: Perhaps a smoker's mellow, obscuring end of bloody horror film

indicators.note: obscuring end of means the last letter of the film is covered by the word for mellow

parts.note: Carrie is the Stephen King horror film with its famous blood-soaked prom
to age is to mellow with time

explanation.surface: A smoker relaxes, missing the ending of a gory horror movie.
explanation.walkthrough: A smoker is an old railway carriage where smoking was allowed; 'Perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoking compartment on a train is an example of a railway coach, hence the 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Bang on 24, for example

parts.note: re means on or concerning
24 across is Rio, a port city

explanation.surface: Something is spot on for clue 24, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bang on' is an idiom for exactly right, but 'Bang' is the definition and 'on' a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The loud sound of a gun firing is a synonym for a bang.

clue.text: Fury of possibly bitter chief technical officer

parts.note: bitter is a type of ale; 'possibly' marks it as an example
CTO is the abbreviation for chief technical officer

explanation.surface: An office tale: the chief technical officer's fury, perhaps from bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pubs 'bitter' is a hoppy beer, here an example of ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Alecto is one of the three Furies, avenging spirits of Greek myth.

clue.text: Salt, maybe an inhabitant of the ocean?

definitions.meaning: to salt food is one way to flavour it, hence maybe
jokingly a son of the sea, someone who lives in it

explanation.surface: A salt, perhaps an old sailor, is described as someone living on the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To flavour food with salt is one way to add taste; the second reading splits into sea plus son.

clue.text: Erstwhile home of Biggs and Orbison, off and on

indicators.note: off and on means every other letter is skipped then kept

explanation.surface: A trivia question pairing the train robber with the singer Roy Orbison, now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Ronnie Biggs, of Britain's 1963 Great Train Robbery, escaped prison and lived for decades in Brazil.
explanation.definitionFit: Rio de Janeiro is the Brazilian city where the fugitive robber lived beyond extradition.

clue.text: Assistant nurse's last to enter hospital chapel site in turn

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital on maps and signs

indicators.note: in turn means the place of worship, with its added letter, is read backwards
to enter means the nurse's letter goes inside the place of worship

parts.note: a temple is a site of worship, like a chapel

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word nurse

explanation.surface: A helper nurse finally goes to the hospital chapel, taking turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A helpmeet is an archaic word for a companion or helper, often a wife.

clue.text: Stone cask over ground, it's used by bakers

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the two pieces read backwards

parts.note: a precious stone is a gem
a tun is a large cask for wine or beer

explanation.surface: A stone barrel tipped over the ground, a baker's tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like the earth under the cask; it belongs to the definition, the powdered spice.
explanation.definitionFit: A grated or powdered spice from a tropical seed, used in cakes and custards.

clue.text: Unusual development in intro to tune by Muse, English rock band

indicators.note: intro to picks the opening letter of tune

parts.note: Erato is the Greek Muse of lyric and love poetry
Genesis is the English rock band of Phil Collins and Peter Gabriel

explanation.surface: An unusual musical evolution: a tune's intro by a muse and an English rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: Muse is also an English rock band, a nice false lead; here it is the Greek goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term for abnormal foetal growth producing malformations, an unusual development.
